name: Glasgow
tagline: Scotland's largest city, a genuinely underrated mix of Victorian grandeur, world-class free museums and a fiercely loyal music scene.
highlight: Wandering Kelvingrove's cathedral-like galleries, from a suspended Spitfire to a real stuffed giraffe, all free to enter.
shortDescription: Scotland's largest city, home to world-class free museums, Victorian architecture and a genuinely legendary live music and nightlife scene.
metaDescription: A Glasgow travel guide: Kelvingrove, Glasgow Cathedral, the Necropolis, food and how to plan a visit to Scotland's largest, most underrated city.
knownFor: Free museums, Victorian architecture, live music

image.file: File:The Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow, Scotland, UK.jpg
image.alt: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum in Glasgow

intro: Glasgow is genuinely Scotland's largest city and its cultural powerhouse, a place of Victorian sandstone grandeur that tends to surprise first-time visitors expecting something rougher around the edges.

It's also genuinely a city of exceptional free museums — Kelvingrove alone holds everything from a Salvador Dalí masterpiece to a suspended Spitfire — alongside a live music scene that has produced a disproportionate share of Britain's best bands.
Most visitors genuinely use Glasgow as a starting point for the wider Highlands, and a couple of days here earns its place on the itinerary well before you head north.

whyVisit.intro: Glasgow's case rests on genuinely world-class free museums and a cultural confidence that rarely gets enough credit.

points.title: Kelvingrove is genuinely one of Europe's best free museums
points.text: A vast collection spanning fine art, natural history and technology, all at no cost.

points.title: The architecture is genuinely spectacular and underrated
points.text: Victorian sandstone grandeur and Charles Rennie Mackintosh's pioneering Art Nouveau designs throughout the city.

points.title: The Necropolis is genuinely a striking, free hilltop walk
points.text: A Victorian garden cemetery with sweeping views back over the cathedral and city.

points.title: Live music here is genuinely the real deal
points.text: A legendary scene that has launched a disproportionate share of Britain's best-known bands.

points.title: It works genuinely well as a gateway to the Highlands
points.text: Trains and rental cars to Loch Lomond and Skye both start here.

attractionsIntro: Glasgow's essential sights combine world-class free museums with striking Victorian and Art Nouveau architecture.

attractions.name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum

image.file: File:The Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow, Scotland, UK.jpg
image.alt: The Victorian facade of Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Europe's best free museums, a vast red sandstone building holding everything from fine art to a suspended Spitfire.
attractions.tip: The genuinely organ recitals, held most days, are worth timing a visit around.

attractions.name: Glasgow Cathedral

image.alt: The main portal of Glasgow Cathedral

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Scotland's few medieval cathedrals to survive the Reformation intact, dating back to the 12th century.
attractions.tip: Genuinely free to enter, and combines well with a walk up to the Necropolis right behind it.

attractions.name: George Square

image.alt: George Square, Glasgow's central civic square

attractions.text: Genuinely the city's civic heart, ringed by grand Victorian buildings and statues of notable Scots including James Watt.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a good landmark for getting oriented before exploring the surrounding Merchant City.

attractions.name: Glasgow Necropolis

image.alt: Glasgow Necropolis, a Victorian hilltop cemetery

attractions.text: A genuinely striking Victorian garden cemetery on a hill above the cathedral, its monuments offering sweeping views over the city.
attractions.tip: Genuinely free to enter, and especially atmospheric at sunset.

attractions.name: Riverside Museum

image.alt: The Riverside Museum on the banks of the River Clyde in Glasgow

attractions.text: A genuinely striking Zaha Hadid-designed building on the Clyde, home to Scotland's transport and travel collection.
attractions.tip: Genuinely combine with the historic tall ship Glenlee, moored right outside.

attractions.name: Glasgow School of Art

image.alt: The Glasgow School of Art building

attractions.text: Genuinely Charles Rennie Mackintosh's most celebrated building, a landmark of Art Nouveau design shaping the city's aesthetic identity.
attractions.tip: Check genuinely ahead for guided tour availability, given the building's ongoing restoration history.

attractions.name: Merchant City

image.alt: The Victorian streets of Glasgow's Merchant City

attractions.text: Genuinely the city's old trading quarter, now full of independent shops, restaurants and Victorian architecture.
attractions.tip: Genuinely one of the best areas for a relaxed evening of dinner and a wander.

thingsToDoIntro: Glasgow genuinely rewards mixing its major museums with a wander through its distinct neighbourhoods.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Kelvingrove's galleries

image.file: File:Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum, Glasgow, interior with giraffe.jpg
image.alt: The interior galleries of Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely absorbing few hours, covering everything from Dutch old masters to natural history displays, entirely free.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely arrive early on weekends — it's one of Scotland's most popular free attractions.

thingsToDo.title: Climb the Necropolis for skyline views

image.alt: Views over Glasgow from the Necropolis hilltop

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding half-hour walk among Victorian monuments, ending with sweeping views over the cathedral and city.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely wear sturdy shoes — the paths can be uneven and occasionally muddy.

thingsToDo.title: Explore the Riverside Museum's vehicles

image.file: File:Wheel detail Riverside Museum Glasgow Scotland.jpg
image.alt: Transport exhibits at the Riverside Museum in Glasgow

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely engaging few hours for any transport enthusiast, from vintage cars to a full recreated 1930s street.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely free to enter, with the historic tall ship Glenlee included nearby.

thingsToDo.title: Stroll Merchant City's Victorian streets

image.alt: The historic streets of Glasgow's Merchant City

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed evening spent browsing independent shops and restaurants along the old trading quarter's grand streets.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a good area to find dinner away from the busiest tourist streets.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph George Square

image.alt: The statue of James Watt in George Square, Glasgow

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely easy stop between sights, ringed by grand Victorian civic buildings and notable statues.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check for seasonal events — the square regularly hosts markets and festivals.

thingsToDo.title: Catch live music in the city
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential part of a Glasgow visit, with venues across the city hosting live acts most nights of the week.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check listings ahead — the scene here is renowned well beyond Scotland.

foodIntro: Glasgow's food genuinely spans serious modern Scottish dining and simple, hearty pub classics at every price point.

foods.name: Haggis, neeps and tatties

image.alt: Haggis served with neeps and tatties, Scotland's national dish

foods.text: Genuinely worth trying at a proper restaurant, Scotland's national dish served across the city at every price point.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional restaurants and pubs throughout the city centre.

foods.name: Scotch whisky

image.file: File:Glen Moray Single Malt Scotch Whisky.jpg
image.alt: A bottle of single malt Scotch whisky

foods.text: Genuinely well served in Glasgow's traditional pubs, with a serious whisky bar scene to match.
foods.whereToTry: Whisky bars and traditional pubs throughout the city.

foods.name: Cullen skink

image.alt: Cullen skink, a traditional Scottish smoked haddock soup

foods.text: A genuinely warming choice on menus across the city, a rich, smoky soup of haddock and potato.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional restaurants and pubs throughout Glasgow.

foods.name: Scottish shortbread
foods.text: A genuinely essential Glasgow café treat, simple and buttery, found in bakeries across the city.
foods.whereToTry: Bakeries and cafés throughout the city centre.

foods.name: Fish and chips

image.file: File:Fish and chips plate with peas.jpg
image.alt: A plate of fish and chips

foods.text: A genuinely reliable classic, sold at chippers across the city, especially popular after a night out.
foods.whereToTry: Chip shops citywide, particularly in the West End.

foods.name: Irn-Bru

image.alt: Bottles of Irn-Bru, Scotland's beloved soft drink

foods.text: Genuinely a beloved Scottish institution, a bright orange, distinctively flavoured soft drink found everywhere.

accommodation.intro: Glasgow genuinely offers accommodation across every budget, concentrated within a compact, walkable city centre.

areas.name: City centre
areas.bestFor: Being genuinely central and walkable to major sights
areas.text: The most convenient base, close to George Square, Merchant City and the main train stations.

areas.name: The West End
areas.bestFor: A genuinely more relaxed, local neighbourhood feel
areas.text: Close to Kelvingrove and the university, with excellent cafés and a livelier evening scene.

gettingThere.intro: Glasgow is genuinely well connected by air and rail, one of Scotland's two main international gateways.

options.text: Genuinely most international routes into western Scotland land here, about 20 minutes from the city centre.
options.detail: A frequent express bus connects the airport to central Glasgow.

options.text: Genuinely fast and direct from Edinburgh, Stirling and Inverness.
options.detail: Glasgow Central and Queen Street stations both sit right in the city centre.

options.text: Genuinely a budget-friendly option from across the UK.
options.detail: Buchanan Bus Station sits a short walk from the city centre.

gettingAround.intro: Glasgow is genuinely compact enough to explore mostly on foot, with good public transport for the rest.

options.text: Genuinely covers the city centre and Merchant City easily.
options.detail: Central Glasgow's main sights sit within a comfortable walking radius of each other.

options.text: Genuinely a quick, simple way to reach the West End and Kelvingrove.
options.detail: Scotland's only underground metro system, small and easy to navigate.

options.text: Genuinely reliable for reaching the Riverside Museum and other outer sights.
options.detail: Frequent services cover the wider city well.

bestTime.headline: May to September for the best weather, though Glasgow works well year-round
bestTime.summary: Glasgow's genuinely museum-heavy, walkable character makes it a viable destination in any season.

seasons.text: Genuinely mild weather and long daylight hours, with fewer crowds than midsummer.
The warmest and busiest season, with festivals and outdoor events.
Genuinely mild with thinner crowds than summer.
Short days and frequent rain, though genuinely atmospheric, with cosy pubs and lower prices.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly — Glasgow's genuinely museum-rich, compact character makes it a workable destination in any season.

days.title: Kelvingrove and the West End
days.summary: Kelvingrove, the Riverside Museum and the West End.

days.title: The Victorian core
days.summary: Glasgow Cathedral, the Necropolis and Merchant City.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Glasgow stay noticeably smoother.
tips: Visit Kelvingrove genuinely early on weekends to beat the crowds.
Take the genuinely Subway for a quick, easy hop between the city centre and the West End.
Budget for genuinely variable restaurant prices — Glasgow spans everything from cheap eats to fine dining.
Wear genuinely comfortable shoes — Glasgow's compact centre still adds up to real walking distances.
Check genuinely live music listings ahead — the scene here draws visitors in its own right.
Pack a proper waterproof layer regardless of season — Glasgow's weather genuinely shifts fast.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Glasgow?
faq.a: Two days genuinely covers the major museums and sights at a comfortable, unrushed pace.

faq.q: Is Glasgow worth visiting before heading to the Highlands?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — its museums add real cultural context, and it's the natural gateway for trains and rental cars heading north.
Moderately, genuinely on par with other major UK cities — its many free museums help keep costs down.
Yes, genuinely — most major sights sit within a comfortable walk of the city centre, with a simple Subway for the rest.
Genuinely its world-class free museums, Victorian and Art Nouveau architecture, and a legendary live music scene.

faq.q: Is Glasgow safer or better than Edinburgh for a first visit?
faq.a: Both are genuinely safe and welcoming — Glasgow offers a grittier, more underrated cultural scene, while Edinburgh leans more historic and picturesque. Many visitors combine both.
